source_text: Videntes elegantem infantem celaverunt mensibus tribus; posuerunt in tibin bitumine in palude. Filia Pharaonis — ecclesia ex gentibus — lavat et misericordiam suscipit. Moyses — lex — intra tibin sordidis Iudaeorum sensibus; ecclesia ad aquas baptismi legem assumit et fortificat. Synagoga mercedem accipit: idolis erubescit. Etiam si Pharao pater fuit, ad aquas legem Dei sumamus. Amen.
pass_a_gloss: Seeing beautiful infant they-hid for-months three; they-placed in basket with-bitumen in marsh. Daughter of-Pharaoh — church from nations — washes and mercy receives. Moses — law — inside basket with-sordid of-Jews senses; church to waters of-baptism law takes-up and strengthens. Synagogue wage receives: at-idols blushes. Even if Pharaoh father was, to waters law of-God let-us-take. Amen.
pass_b_english: [[Seeing the child was beautiful, they hid him three months >> Bible:Exodus 2:2]], then set him in a bitumen-sealed basket by the river. Pharaoh’s daughter — the church gathered from the nations — comes to the waters to wash from her father’s house, [[hears “Daughter, forget your father’s house” >> Bible:Psalm 45:11]], and receives the infant with mercy. Moses names the Law: shut in cheap coverings of literal Jewish reading until the church takes him from the marsh into royal rooms. Grown strong, the veil of the letter lifts and solid food appears [[Hebrews 5:12-14 >> Bible:Hebrews 5:12-14]]. The synagogue’s “wage” is that, seeing Gentiles worship one God, she blushes to serve idols still [[Deuteronomy 32:21 >> Bible:Deuteronomy 32:21]]. Though Pharaoh once fathered us in evil works, when we come to the waters let us take up a great Moses — nothing small, everything spiritual — and ask Christ to reveal how great he is. [[To him be glory forever. Amen >> Bible:1 Peter 4:11]].
